memories.content: Specify the order and recipients for reporting serious discomfort during the study.
Field staff rely on a pre-defined contact sequence when serious discomfort is reported.
Establish criteria for halting the use of a design alternative if recurring severe errors appear during formative evaluation.
Do not include a design alternative halted for safety reasons in subsequent evaluation iterations without modification.
Even in controlled environments, delayed prototype recovery procedures increase session interruption time and alter data collection conditions for the same task.
Specify in one sentence the user population and actual usage environment to which the design knowledge applies.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through the specified target population and environment.
Specify the workflow, technical infrastructure, and operational-authority conditions that must match before applying the design guidelines at another field site.
The transferability of field design knowledge depends not only on user characteristics but also on workflow and technological–organizational infrastructure.
The user tends to apply results confirmed at one deployment site to all similar organizations.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational concerns. The reference covers discomfort escalation, safety-based evaluation controls, and prototype-recovery effects; the compared frame covers generalization boundaries, transfer conditions, and overgeneralization behavior. No shared or scope-dependent claim is established.

relations.reason: The reference memories express complementary normative and operational forms of one reporting-sequence claim, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Serious discomfort is handled through a specified reporting order and recipient sequence used by field staff.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only claim about the threshold for stopping an alternative.
relations.summary: Formative evaluation requires criteria for halting a design alternative when severe errors recur.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only rule governing subsequent reuse after a safety halt.
relations.summary: A design alternative halted for safety reasons must be modified before inclusion in later evaluation iterations.

relations.reason: This reference-only causal observation concerns session continuity and data conditions, independently of the other claims.
relations.summary: Delayed prototype recovery increases interruption time and changes data-collection conditions even in controlled environments.

relations.reason: The compared memories state procedural and evaluative aspects of one generalization-boundary claim, with no reference counterpart.
relations.summary: The applicable user population and actual usage environment define the boundary through which reviewers judge generalization.

relations.reason: The compared memories jointly specify one transferability claim and its required contextual dimensions.
relations.summary: Transfer to another field site depends on matching workflow, technical infrastructure, and organizational or operational-authority conditions, not only user characteristics.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only behavioral observation about overgeneralization.
relations.summary: The user tends to apply findings from one deployment site across all similar organizations.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame defines population and environment boundaries, field-site transfer conditions, and a tendency to overgeneralize findings across organizations.
reports.reference_only: The reference specifies serious-discomfort reporting, safety-based halting and reuse controls, and the effect of delayed prototype recovery on sessions and data conditions.
